Issue Reading note
Consolidated margins understate the ad business FoA is 98.9% of revenue but RL absorbed 18% of FY2025 costs and lost $19,193M. FoA's segment margin was 51.6% in FY2025 against 41.4% consolidated. Segment reporting began in Q4 2021 with history recast only to FY2019, so FY2016-FY2018 exist only on a consolidated basis.
The latest quarter breaks the FY2025 run-rate Revenue growth rose from 22% (FY2025) to 33% (Q1 2026) and 28% (Q2 2026), while FoA margin declined to 38.8% in Q2 2026, capex reached 51.1% of revenue and free cash flow was $784M. Every FY2025 margin and cash figure here is shown beside the H1 2026 figure.
Post-Q2 events come from press The 26 August 2026 attorney-general settlement and its expected ~$10bn Q3 2026 accrual, the September 2026 Muse subscription launch and the 21 September price move are known only from press reports. FY2026 GAAP operating income in Section 17 depends on the accrual.
Core ads and frontier-model spend are one segment Meta Superintelligence Labs, the 2025-26 AI talent packages and third-party AI token costs are booked inside FoA, and Meta does not split capex or cost between ads ranking and frontier-model training. The FoA margin decline since 2024 cannot be divided between the two.
  • Ad impressions and average price per ad are disclosed only as year-over-year growth rates, never as levels. Family daily active people (DAP) is an estimate with a stated error margin of about 3%, the same size as the +3% growth reported for June 2026.
  • Revenue by user geography (earnings decks) and by customer billing address (10-K Note 2) differ by up to $14.6bn a year for a region; both are used and labelled.
  • RL revenue is not split by product, and Meta's economics on glasses sold by EssilorLuxottica are undisclosed, so every RL unit figure is an estimate with its range.

1. Business description, model and unit economics

FoA segment margin was 51.6% in FY2025 and 43.3% in H1 2026 (38.8% in Q2 2026, after $2.4bn of legal charges and $1.18bn of severance). How impressions per person split between more time spent and more ads per minute, and which apps account for the growth, are undisclosed (Section 20, items 1 and 5).

Meta sells advertising on apps used daily by 3.60bn people (June 2026): Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and Threads. Marketers, most of them small businesses buying self-serve, bid in a real-time auction for each impression; revenue is ad impressions times average price per ad.▪ A small and fast-growing second stream charges businesses for WhatsApp messages and consumers for subscriptions. Reality Labs sells AI glasses (with EssilorLuxottica), Quest headsets and Horizon Store content, and loses about $19bn a year. Meta reports two segments (10-K FY2025, Note 15).

1.1 Family of Apps

Who pays, and how price is set. The buyer is a performance marketer allocating a budget against measured return on ad spend, choosing between Meta, Google Search and YouTube, Amazon, TikTok and AppLovin. Meta sets no list price. Each impression clears in an auction, so price rises when advertisers expect more conversions per impression. There are no multi-year contracts or take-or-pay terms; deferred revenue was $1,080M at December 2025, 0.5% of revenue, and receivables ran about 36 days (10-K FY2025, Note 1 and Note 2).▪ No customer reached 10% of revenue in 2023-2025. Advantage+, the automated campaign product, passed a $75bn annual revenue run rate in Q2 2026, about 32% of annualised ad revenue (Q2 2026 call).

The revenue equation, reconciled. Advertising revenue = impressions × average price per ad, and impressions = DAP × time per person × ads per unit of time. Compounding the disclosed growth rates for 2020 through 2025 (from the 2019 level) gives impressions up 2.77x and price per ad up 2%, a product of 2.83x against actual ad revenue growth of 2.82x ($69,655M to $196,175M). Almost all six-year growth was volume.▪

Three lines are hypotheses with no reported revenue: the Muse Spark API, Meta Business Agents and the sale of surplus compute, about which Zuckerberg said Meta is "getting a lot of offers for compute at a significant premium over what we paid for it" (Q2 2026 call).

China-based advertisers. FY2025 revenue billed to Asia-Pacific customer addresses was $53,817M (10-K FY2025, Note 2) against $39,259M of revenue from Asia-Pacific users (Q2 2026 deck, slide 3, sum of 2025 quarters). The $14,558M gap, 7.2% of revenue, is billed in Asia-Pacific for impressions shown elsewhere, so it is a minimum for cross-border advertising aimed at Western users. Press reports put China-based advertisers at about 10-11% of 2024 revenue [web, unverified] (Yahoo Finance, accessed 2026-09-23). The 10-K says Meta generates "meaningful revenue from a small number of resellers serving advertisers based in China." The range is 7-11% of revenue, about $15-22bn on FY2025 [estimate: billing-versus-user gap as the minimum; press figure as the maximum].▪

FoA employee compensation rose 28% in 2025 to $39,943M and 45% in H1 2026 to $26,650M while company headcount declined 1% y/y to 75,472▪; the CFO attributed the increase to "technical hires ... particularly AI talent" (Q2 2026 call). The 2026 expense guide of $165-169bn, less RL costs of $21.5-22.5bn, puts FoA costs at $142.5-147.5bn, +48% to +53%, and with consensus revenue gives a 2026 FoA incremental margin of 3-13% [estimate: guide less RL; BBG FY2026 revenue $254.1bn less ~$2.3bn RL].▪ In 2023 FoA costs declined $1.65bn after a 22% headcount cut; the 2026 cost base is dominated by depreciation, cloud contracts and $349.31bn of non-cancelable commitments, which do not respond to headcount decisions.

Who books the glasses sale. EssilorLuxottica sold "above 7 million" Meta glasses in 2025 and said AI-glasses revenue diluted its own gross margin because of the "higher weight of the AI-glasses revenue" (invisionmag, accessed 2026-09-23 [web]). A dilution that shows in its own gross margin means EssilorLuxottica books the retail or wholesale sale of most units, and Meta's RL revenue includes only Meta's share plus Meta.com sales.▪ The contract terms are undisclosed.

Two estimates of Meta's revenue per glasses unit: - Residual from RL revenue: $2,207M less Quest hardware (2.3-3.9m units at $250-330 net, two tracker-based unit estimates) and $0.2-0.3bn of store and accessories, divided by 7m+ glasses, gives about $95-170 per unit [estimate: residual; Quest units from IDC's 5.6m for 2024 and 1.7m for Q1-Q3 2025]. - Third-party unit model: AR Insider allocates $181M of Q1 2026 RL revenue to 1.10m Ray-Ban Meta units, about $165 per unit (arinsider.co, 2026-05-06 [web]), a method its author calls "educated but up for debate".

With a separate incremental estimate of $150-200 a unit, the combined range is about $95-200 (Section 19). Against a blended 2025 retail price of about $330-400, Meta books roughly 25-50% of retail value per unit.▪

2. Key technologies and technical differentiators

Meta's technical advantage is concentrated in the ranking and recommendation systems that choose which post and which ad each of 3.6bn daily users sees.▪ The algorithms are published research that TikTok, Google and AppLovin also run. The difference comes from combining four inputs in one company: first-party engagement data, closed-loop conversion data from millions of advertisers, the compute to train large recommendation models, and an annual budget process that funds and measures dozens of ranking launches a year.

Ads ranking stack. An auction runs in stages within milliseconds. Andromeda narrows "a pool of tens of millions of ads to the few thousand we consider showing someone" and enabled "a 10,000x increase in the complexity of models we use for ads retrieval" (Q4 2024 call). GEM, the Generative Ads Recommendation Model, is trained on ads and organic engagement together and is too large to serve, so its learning is transferred into smaller runtime models. The GPUs used to train it doubled in Q4 2025, when Meta called it "the first time we have found a recommendation model architecture that can scale with similar efficiency as LLMs" (Q4 2025 call). An adaptive ranking model routes only high-conversion requests to "LLM scale model complexity of 1 trillion parameters" (Q1 2026 call). Lattice replaced many per-surface models with fewer large ones; about 100 were retired and 200 more are being consolidated (Q3 2025 call). The Meta Generative Recommender, deployed in Q2 2026, predicts "the best ad for each person" instead of scoring each candidate separately (Q2 2026 call).

Each reported lift is small: 3-6% conversion gains on specific surfaces in 2025, and 8.3% more ad clicks and 15.7% more conversions on Facebook from user-understanding models in Q2 2026 (earnings calls).▪ Susan Li said the gains "turned out to be more additive than we expected", and in the same appearance that Meta's experiments on the advertiser-budget loop were "not statistically significant" (Morgan Stanley TMT, 4 March 2026). The lifts are management measurements and cannot be checked independently.

The data are hard to replicate because no Western rival holds a feed and an ad base of this size in one company, and because Meta rebuilt conversion data on-platform (click-to-message and lead ads) after Apple's ATT removed cross-app tracking. Competitors show what the techniques alone achieve. TikTok built an interest-graph recommender with no social graph and forced Meta into Reels, which was a revenue headwind in 2022-2023 and reached a $50bn run rate by Q3 2025. AppLovin's Axon lifted its share of e-commerce ad budgets to 11.1% in Q2 2026, up 169bp from late 2025, in a 30-advertiser Jefferies survey that found the shift came from incremental budgets (Investing.com, accessed 2026-09-23 [web]).

Advantage+. The run rate rose from $10bn (Q3 2023, shopping campaigns) to over $20bn (Q4 2024), $60bn (Q3 2025) and over $75bn (Q2 2026). The step between Q4 2024 and Q3 2025 coincided with a scope change from shopping-only to all end-to-end objectives and with automation becoming the default in campaign setup, so run-rate growth mostly measures product consolidation.▪ How much is incremental advertiser spend and how much moved from manual campaigns is undisclosed. Lead campaigns on Advantage+ show 14% lower cost per lead (Q3 2025 call), and 9m businesses use at least one generative creative tool (Q2 2026 call).

Organic recommendation. Over half of recommended Instagram feed content is less than a day old, double a year earlier, and every public Instagram Reels and feed post is labelled by an LLM for topic and tone (Q2 2026 call). The shift to recommended content is visible in Meta's own trial exhibit: video rose from about 11% of US Facebook time in January 2015 to about 53% in January 2025 [deck: FTC v. Meta opening statement 2025-04-14, slide 38].

Frontier models. Llama 4 (April 2025) disappointed: an unreleased chat-tuned variant ranked second on LMArena while the public model ranked 32nd (The Register, 2025-04-08 [web]), and the "Behemoth" teacher model was delayed (Axios, 2025-05-15 [web]) and not released. Meta formed Meta Superintelligence Labs under Alexandr Wang after its Scale AI investment. Muse Spark (April 2026), the first MSL model and Meta's first frontier model withheld as closed weights, scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index behind Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6, and 1427 on the agentic GDPval-AA benchmark against 1676 for GPT-5.4▪ (Artificial Analysis, 2026-04-08 [web]). The FY2025 10-K added: "We have not released everything we have developed historically and expect to continue training a combination of open and closed models going forward." Meta AI had over 1bn monthly users before Muse, "despite not being on a state-of-the-art foundation model" (Susan Li, MS TMT 2026), which puts the source of that audience in distribution across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. The Muse Spark API has been in public preview since July 2026 at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens on OpenRouter (openrouter.ai, accessed 2026-09-23 [web]); no API revenue is disclosed.

Infrastructure and silicon. Prometheus, described as "the world's first gigawatt-plus cluster", comes online in 2026, and Hyperion in Louisiana can scale to 5GW (Q2 2025 call). Meta signed a 6GW agreement for custom AMD MI450-based GPUs from 2H 2026 with a warrant for up to 160m AMD shares (AMD, 2026-02-24 [web]), a 1GW MTIA commitment with Broadcom (CNBC, 2026-04-14 [web]) and an expanded NVIDIA deal. MTIA has run ranking inference since 1H 2024. Meta scrapped its first inference chip in 2022 and, as reported in February 2026, its most advanced training chip (Dataconomy, 2026-02-27 [web]). Frontier training runs on merchant GPUs, and Meta also rents Google TPUs and pays "third-party AI token costs" (Q2 2026 call). The infrastructure is a cost and supply-access advantage; hyperscalers and neoclouds sell comparable capacity, and Meta buys from them.▪

WhatsApp. The encryption and messaging technology is licensed and widely available. The asset is the network of more than 2bn daily users (Q4 2025 call), where contacts and groups create switching costs. Business AI weekly conversations went from 1m at the start of 2026 to 10m in Q1 2026, and business AIs are "currently free for most businesses" (Q1 2026 call).

Reality Labs. Meta Ray-Ban Display has a monocular display at 42 pixels per degree and up to 5,000 nits; the Neural Band detects wrist muscle signals for silent input (Connect 2025 transcript). The glasses lead comes from the EssilorLuxottica brand and retail partnership, five years of shipping product since Ray-Ban Stories (2021) and EMG research from the 2019 CTRL-labs acquisition. Google and Samsung announced Android XR audio glasses with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster for fall 2026 (9to5Google, 2026-05-19 [web]).

Roadmap exposure is low for the core ads stack, which ships on the cadence described on prior calls, and high for everything else: "Our focus this year is validating the model architectures ... before we scale them out in future years" (Q1 2026 call, on LLM-native recommenders), and on personal agents "we're going to ship this at some point soon ... And we haven't done that yet" (Zuckerberg, Q2 2026 call).

3. Competitive advantages and moat assessment

How much of the 2026 cost increase and capex serves core ads ranking and how much serves frontier-model training is unknown (Section 20, item 2). FoA returns cannot be divided between a lower return in the ad system and spending on a separate frontier-AI program.

3.1 Family of Apps

The ad business has an advantage that has survived well-funded attacks and earns returns far above its cost of capital, and that now requires heavy reinvestment to defend.▪ It withstood Google+ (2011-2019), Snapchat's Stories (Meta copied the format in 2016; Snap lost 9.0% of revenue at the operating line in FY2025) and Apple's App Tracking Transparency (Meta sized the 2022 headwind at about $10bn; ad revenue went from $114,934M in 2021 to $113,642M in 2022, then grew 16% in 2023). Against TikTok, which took share of user time, Meta has kept growing ad revenue, +27% in Q2 2026. FoA operating margin was 51.6% in FY2025 against 40.7% for Google Services, and FoA after-tax return on invested capital was about 43-46% [estimate: FoA operating income taxed at 21% over average consolidated invested capital, less a 0-5% RL share] against a cost of capital of about 10%.▪

Capex including finance-lease principal rose from 16.3% of revenue in 2021 to 35.9% in FY2025, and the 2026 guide of $130-145bn is 51-57% of consensus revenue. Consolidated ROIC declined from 44.0% (2021) to 35.2% (FY2025) and 28.6% on a trailing basis to June 2026, and the return on capital added in 2025 alone was about 17%.▪ In Q2 2026 FoA margin was 38.8%, below Google Services' 41.8% for the first time since at least 2020; before that quarter's charges it was about 43-45%.▪

The advantage used to come from a friend graph with near-zero marginal cost, and that source is shrinking.▪ Meta's own trial exhibit shows friends' content declining to 17% of Facebook time and 7% of Instagram time in 2025 [deck: FTC v. Meta opening statement 2025-04-14, slides 20-21], and Judge Boasberg held in November 2025 that TikTok and YouTube are substitutes for Facebook and Instagram (CNBC, 2025-11-18 [web]). What still separates Meta is the combination of 3.6bn daily users, owned inventory that pays no traffic-acquisition cost, and conversion data from millions of self-serve advertisers.▪ The ranking quality built on that combination improves with compute, which Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and ByteDance can also buy.

Business-model analogues. - Alphabet, Google Services. Owned attention, a self-serve auction and machine-learned ranking funded by advertiser conversion data. The analogy breaks on intent: search captures stated demand while Meta creates demand in a feed, and Google pays traffic-acquisition costs ($59,926M in FY2025) that Meta does not. FoA's 11-14 point margin premium over Google Services in 2020-2025 (excluding 2022) is consistent with that cost.▪ - Tencent (Weixin). A messaging and social network with daily reach, monetised through ads, services and business messaging; the closest precedent for WhatsApp paid messaging and business agents. It breaks because Tencent also earns payments and gaming revenue under China's regulatory regime. - AppLovin. The ranking half of Meta's advantage on its own: a 75.8% FY2025 operating margin and ROIC of about 92% on a machine-learned ad network. It breaks because AppLovin owns no audience and monetises other publishers' apps, at 2.7% of Meta's revenue.

Management claims: Meta's 10-K frames the business around competition: "We face significant competition in every aspect of our business." The advantage claims come on calls. Susan Li: "our distribution advantages will give us the opportunity to serve AI products that are valuable for everyone, both our 3.6 billion users and millions of businesses. This should be true regardless of whether our models are on the frontier" (Q2 2026 call). Zuckerberg: "being the most efficient at how we engineer, invest and partner to build our infrastructure will become a strategic advantage" (Q4 2025 call). In the FTC trial Meta argued the opposite about attention, that it competes with TikTok, YouTube and iMessage and must "evolve or die" [deck: FTC v. Meta 2025-04-14, slides 5 and 22].

External sources: Morgan Stanley (Overweight, 30 July 2026) calls the core social moat "strengthening". Goldman Sachs (30 July) sees "evidence of near-term ROIC" in core ads with "lack of visibility into LT compute spend". J.P. Morgan (Neutral until its 10 September upgrade) cited "limited visibility into newer forms of AI monetization". eMarketer forecasts Meta's 2026 worldwide ad revenue at $243.46bn, 26.8% of global ad spending, passing Google's $239.54bn net of traffic-acquisition cost (Marketing Dive, 2026-04-14 [web]). Practitioner data are thinner: Triple Whale's reported 2025 median e-commerce return on ad spend was 1.86 for Meta and 2.21 for TikTok (digitalapplied.com, accessed 2026-09-23 [web, low confidence, secondary]).

Ground-up view: Users pay with time and advertisers bid for impressions, with Meta controlling supply through ad load. Three conditions let the business earn excess returns: a leading share of mobile attention, conversion performance ahead of rivals, and TAC-free inventory. The first is contested (the court finding, TikTok). The second now requires frontier-scale compute, which exposes the excess return to a rising capital bill; minimum efficient scale in 2026 is $130-145bn of capex plus $349.31bn of commitments, which keeps Snap, Pinterest and Reddit from matching Meta's conversion performance and does not stop Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon or ByteDance.▪ The third comes from owning the apps. User switching costs are low and falling, because recommended entertainment needs no friend graph; network effects protect WhatsApp and Messenger more than the Facebook and Instagram feeds. Advertiser switching costs are low contractually and rising operationally through the Conversions API, pixel data and Advantage+ automation, and a denser auction matches small budgets better. Apple, Google and EU regulators hold the power over ad signals.

Return on invested capital.

ROIC = operating income × (1 − 21%) ÷ average invested capital, where invested capital = equity + debt + operating lease liabilities − cash − current marketable securities. A uniform 21% rate is used across companies so one-off tax items do not drive the comparison; META's FY2025 reported rate was 30%, or 13% excluding the One Big Beautiful Bill Act charge (38.8% ROIC at 13%). Cost of capital about 10% (risk-free about 4.3%, beta about 1.2, equity premium 5%). ROIIC = change in NOPAT ÷ change in invested capital.

3.2 Reality Labs

Reality Labs has no durable competitive advantage in the financial sense.▪ It has lost money in every year since segment reporting began, the loss grew from $4,503M (2019) to $19,193M (2025), and costs were 9.7x revenue in 2025. RL revenue grew about 14% a year from 2020 to 2025 while RL costs grew about 23% a year; since 2022 the rates are 0.7% and 10.5%.▪ Meta does hold a real market position: IDC puts its smart-glasses share at 69.2% in Q1 2026 and 68.7% in Q2 2026 (mixed-news.com, accessed 2026-09-23 [web]). That position is based on the exclusive design, manufacturing and optical-retail partnership with EssilorLuxottica and on a lead in on-device AI, displays and EMG input funded by nearly $100bn of cumulative spend.▪ Share has not produced returns: the VR market shrank 14% in H1 2025 and 18% in Q2 2026 (Counterpoint [web]), and Quest pricing moved down (the Quest 2 rise to $399 in 2022 was reversed in 2023; Quest Pro was cut from $1,499 to $999 within four months [web]). In glasses, EssilorLuxottica books most of the retail sale and Meta books about $95-200 a unit [estimate, Section 1.2]. The glasses position is an option on a profitable business; it becomes one only if RL revenue scales with glasses units and the loss declines as management guided ("this will likely be the peak as we start to gradually reduce our losses going forward", Q4 2025 call).

Business-model analogues (first mover in a new consumer-device category, hardware near cost, value expected from a service layer, facing platform owners with larger installed bases): - Fitbit (public 2015-2021): an early share leader whose share and margins were competed away by a platform owner (Apple) and a low-cost maker (Xiaomi). It breaks because Fitbit had no parent subsidy and earned positive gross margins at the start. - GoPro: a category-defining device whose leadership did not stop revenue decline (5-year CAGR −6.1%) and losses (FY2025 operating margin −12.8%). It breaks because GoPro never owned an AI or social layer. - Garmin is the counter-case: niche wearable brands at 58.7% gross margin, 25.9% operating margin and about 25% ROIC. RL would need Garmin-like unit margins on glasses at 10m-plus units.

Management claims: "Sales of our glasses more than tripled last year, and we think that they're some of the fastest-growing consumer electronics in history" (Q4 2025 call); Meta Ray-Ban Display "sold out in almost every store within 48 hours" (Q3 2025 call); profitability arrives when glasses "reach many hundreds of millions or billions of people" (Q3 2025 call). The 10-K concedes "relatively limited experience with consumer hardware products" and dependence on mobile platforms that "do not necessarily provide our products with the same levels of interoperability that they provide to their own competing products."

External sources: IDC forecasts 13.6m display-free glasses units and $5.1bn of revenue in 2026, "moderating as pricing pressure intensifies" [web]; IDC's Q2 2026 XR growth was +35.3%, "a sharp cooling from the 130.2% growth" [web]. EssilorLuxottica reached its 10m-units-a-year capacity target early and is discussing about 20m [web]. Entrants: Google and Samsung Android XR glasses with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster in fall 2026; Apple glasses reported for a late-2027 launch after a WWDC 2027 unveil (MacRumors and 9to5Mac reports of May and July 2026 [web]); Alibaba, Xiaomi and RayNeo in China. Apple halted Vision Pro production in 2025 after about 390,000 launch-period units (The Register, 2026-01-02 [web]).

Ground-up view: Consumer-electronics profits go to platform owners with large installed bases and to low-cost volume makers. Meta owns no phone platform, so its glasses depend on iOS and Android pairing. EssilorLuxottica controls the largest frame brands, optical retail and manufacturing; Meta holds a partnership and about 3% of the equity, and Google copied the structure with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster at a lower brand tier. Switching costs are low on 2-4 year replacement cycles, the AI assistant layer is portable, and Horizon's social VR has not shown compounding engagement. The spending barrier is real: $96,725M of RL losses since 2019, funded by FoA operating income of $102,469M in FY2025 alone. That barrier deters entrants but earns no return.

4. Competitive landscape and market sizing

4.1 Family of Apps (digital advertising)

Among US-listed ad sellers Meta has the largest audience and the second-largest filed ad revenue, and it adds the most dollars each year. Its ad revenue was 57.3% of Google advertising's in FY2020, 66.6% in FY2025 and 72.7% in Q2 2026.▪ Net of Alphabet's traffic-acquisition costs (a 20.3% rate in FY2025), Meta was 84% of Google advertising in FY2025 and about 91% in Q2 2026 [estimate: FY2025 TAC rate applied to Q2 2026].

Meta's share of the pool rose 1.3 points in five years while Alphabet's declined 5.8 points and Amazon's rose 4.0.▪ The pool's HHI was about 3,700 in FY2025 and 4,100 in FY2020 [estimate: sum of squared shares], both above the 2,500 threshold US agencies use for "highly concentrated". Of the FY2024-to-FY2025 increase for the three scale sellers ($78.1bn), Meta accounted for $35.5bn (45.5%), Google $30.1bn and Amazon $12.4bn; in Q2 2026 Meta accounted for $12.8bn of $27.2bn (47.3%).▪

Third-party sizing. WPP Media puts 2026 global ad revenue at $1.3tn (+8.9%), with Alphabet, Meta and Amazon at 57.6% outside China, and expects social media growth to "decelerate to single digits from 2027", partly from chatbot competition (WPP Media, midyear 2026 [web]). eMarketer's 2026 shares imply a digital denominator of about $0.91tn [estimate: $243.46bn ÷ 26.8%], with ByteDance at 7.9% (TikTok 4.8%). WARC forecasts Meta's 2026 ad revenue at about $240bn (+22.3%) and 2027 growth of 12.1% (Telemedia, 2026-05-11 [web]).

Bottom-up social and short-video pool, 2025 (ex-China). Meta $196.2bn (filed), TikTok about $33bn (third-party estimate [web]), YouTube $40.4bn (filed), Snap $5.2bn, Pinterest $4.2bn, Reddit $2.1bn, LinkedIn Marketing Solutions about $5-7bn and X about $2-2.5bn [estimates]. Meta's share is about 78-79% excluding YouTube and 67-68% including it; the HHI is about 6,400 and 5,000 on the two definitions [estimate].▪

Who sets price. The auction sets price, and Meta controls supply through ad load. Volume and price have risen together since 2024, so demand has grown faster than inventory. Google's cost-per-click rose 7% in FY2025 on 6% more paid clicks (GOOGL 10-K FY2025), against Meta's price +9% on impressions +12%. Customer power is low; supplier power is held by Apple and Google, which take no share of Meta's ad dollar but set the signal rules on the devices where "substantially all" DAP access FoA (10-K FY2025).▪

Peer scale and KPI comparison. User counts are on each company's own basis (Meta DAP de-duplicates across four apps; Snap DAU; Reddit logged-in and logged-out DAUq; Pinterest MAU only), so they are not strictly comparable.

FY2025 revenue per daily user on each company's basis: Meta about $57, Reddit about $19, Snap about $13, Pinterest about $7 per monthly user [estimate: revenue ÷ average users]. Meta leads on reach and revenue per user, trails Google on gross filed ad revenue, and at the Q2 2026 growth gap (27% against 14%) would match Google's gross ad revenue in about three years [estimate: 0.727 × (1.27/1.144)^3 ≈ 0.99].

Share counter-evidence, ordered by revenue at risk. - TikTok and short video. TikTok's ex-China ad revenue grew about 40% in 2025 to about $33bn [web estimate], about 17% of Meta's ad revenue.▪ Friends' content is a declining share of Meta's own time spent (Section 3.1). TikTok's US business moved to the TikTok USDS joint venture on 22 January 2026 (Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX 15% each, ByteDance 19.9%) [web], which removed the ban risk that had shifted budgets toward Meta. Reels "monetizes at a lower rate than our Feed and Stories products" (10-K FY2025). In Meta's natural-experiment exhibits YouTube and TikTok were the closest outside substitutes in every test, and Snap gained 0.5-4% [deck: FTC v. Meta 2025-04-14, slides 28-32]. - Amazon and retail media. Amazon rose from 7.5% to 11.5% of the pool in five years with closed-loop purchase data Meta lacks after ATT, and it competes for the same e-commerce budgets that were Meta's largest source of growth in FY2025 and Q2 2026. - AI assistants. OpenAI launched ChatGPT ads on 9 February 2026 and reported a $1bn annualised run rate about 200 days later (CNBC, 2026-08-31 [web]), about 0.4% of Meta's annualised ad revenue. - China-based advertisers. At least 7% of revenue (Section 1.1), exposed to tariffs and the end of the US de minimis exemption on 2 May 2025, after which management said Asia-based exporters reduced US spend (Q1 2025 call). - Regulation of the ad product. In the EU the DMA decision on "subscription for no ads" and the less-personalised-ads option could have "a significant impact to our European business and revenue" (10-K FY2025); Europe was $46,569M of FY2025 billing revenue (23%). The FTC appealed the November 2025 ruling on 20 January 2026 and still seeks divestiture of Instagram and WhatsApp. - Smaller social platforms. Reddit (+61% in Q2 2026) and Pinterest (+18%) together had Q2 2026 revenue of $1,985M, 3.3% of Meta's ad revenue.

Meta's trial exhibit shows its share of time spent at about 85% in the FTC's proposed market, below 60% with TikTok, about 30% with YouTube and below 20% with iMessage and other apps [deck: FTC v. Meta 2025-04-14, slides 67-72]. Against a 67-79% share of social ad dollars, Meta earns far more per unit of attention than TikTok or YouTube on any of those time-share definitions.

4.2 Reality Labs (glasses and headsets)

RL competes in two markets moving in opposite directions: AI glasses, where Meta leads by volume and the category grew 2-4x a year, and VR headsets, where Meta leads a market that is shrinking and its share is declining.▪

AI glasses, sized bottom-up. Omdia counted 8.7m AI-glasses units in 2025, of which Meta shipped about 7.4m (85.2%)▪ (Omdia, 2026-03-05 [web]). At a blended retail price of $350-380 that is about $3.0-3.3bn of consumer spend [estimate: units × ASP]. IDC forecasts 13.6m units and $5.1bn in 2026 and 27.3m units by 2030 with ASP declining from about $376 to about $229 (IDC, updated 2026-07-01 [web]); 27.3m × $229 is about $6.3bn of 2030 hardware [estimate], and IDC's own 2030 figure for optical see-through glasses is $7.1bn. Omdia forecasts more than 15m units in 2026.

In display AI glasses, Meta Ray-Ban Display shipped 84,000 of about 730,000 units in 2025 (about 12%), and Chinese vendors (Rokid, Alibaba, Even Realities) held 71% (Omdia [web]).▪ Counterpoint gives Meta 94% of display-less shipments and 37% of display glasses in H1 2026, behind Rokid's 41% (9to5Mac, 2026-09-21 [web]). Meta and EssilorLuxottica set the Western price at about $299-499 for audio and camera glasses and $799 for Display.

VR and MR headsets. About 4.3m standalone headsets shipped in 2025 plus about 0.45m PC VR [web, low confidence], a hardware pool of about $1.5-2.0bn a year [estimate: 4.3-4.75m × $350-420]. VR shipments declined in 2022, 2023 and 2024 (2024 −12%), 14% in H1 2025 and 18% in Q2 2026 (Counterpoint via vr.org [web]), part of it after Meta raised Quest prices 12.5-20% in April 2026 on memory costs.

Meta's 2025 RL cost base of $21.4bn was 4.2x IDC's 2026 smart-glasses revenue forecast of $5.1bn and about 12x the global VR/MR hardware pool [estimate].▪ The roughly $15bn of 2026 wearables spend is 4.5-5.0x 2025 glasses consumer spend; the full RL cost base is 6.5-7.1x [estimate]. Even IDC's full 2030 glasses pool (about $6.3bn on units × ASP, or $7.1bn on IDC's own optical see-through figure) would fall short of current RL costs at hardware margins, so loss reduction depends on cost decisions or on services revenue ("additional services from the AI", Q3 2025 call).

Share counter-evidence. - Google and Samsung Android XR (fall 2026): the first entrant with a phone OS, a frontier model and an eyewear partner, pairing with both iOS and Android. IDC names Android XR as the main pressure on Meta's lead. - Chinese display-glasses vendors: 71% of display AI glasses, the generation management calls "the next generation of how this product evolves" (Q1 2026 call, Li), in a China market Meta does not sell into directly. - Headset share erosion after Meta's own price rise: 72% to 54% in four quarters; enterprise and robot-teleoperation demand, where Pico is strong, is the resilient part of VR. - Apple glasses: reported for late 2027; Apple controls the iOS interoperability the 10-K names as a constraint. - Partner concentration: glasses volume depends on EssilorLuxottica for brands, capacity and retail, and EssilorLuxottica also works with Applied Materials on optical systems [web].

5. Value chain and profit pools

Meta has two chains. In FoA, advertisers pay Meta almost the whole ad dollar, and the cost side is an AI-infrastructure chain of TSMC, NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, the memory makers, builders, utilities and third-party clouds. Apple and Google are outside the chain, taking nothing from the ad dollar and controlling the signals that set targeting quality.▪ In RL, EssilorLuxottica designs, manufactures and sells the glasses, and Meta supplies electronics, software, Meta AI and the R&D.

The advertiser's dollar. Advertisers pay "either directly or through their relationships with advertising agencies or resellers" (10-K FY2025, Item 7). Agency fees are paid by the advertiser on top of media. Traffic-acquisition cost is limited to Audience Network and is not broken out. Apple and Google take only App Store and Play fees on in-app purchases such as Meta Verified.

Where Meta's dollar goes, 2026 run-rate. Capex at the $137.5bn guide midpoint is about 54 cents per dollar of consensus 2026 revenue ($254.1bn). Capex is cash paid to suppliers and reaches the income statement later as depreciation, so the rows do not sum to $1.

From December 2025 to June 2026 gross servers and network rose $21.6bn, buildings $5.5bn and construction in progress $29.8bn against H1 capex of $50.92bn (10-Q Q2 2026, Note 6), so servers are at least 42% of additions. In 2026 accelerator vendors earn gross profit of about 13-20 cents per Meta revenue dollar on Meta's purchases [estimate: 18-26c × 70-75% vendor gross margin], equal to roughly 40-60% of Meta's own operating profit▪; they book it at shipment, and Meta recovers its outlay over a 5.5-year server life.

The binding constraint. Compute capacity and its funding are the binding constraint today, and the scarcest input, judged by who is earning margin, is memory, then foundry and packaging.▪

Micron's largest strategic customer agreements are take-or-pay with a ceiling that "approximates the market price in the second calendar quarter of 2026, and a floor price" for the term (MU 10-Q, Strategic Customer Agreements). In Q1 2026 Meta raised its 2026 capex guide by $10bn at both ends, and Li attributed the raise to "higher component pricing ... and to a lesser extent, additional data center costs" (Q1 2026 call), so more than half of the raise was component inflation.

Lead times run two to four years: Hyperion leases commence in 2029 (10-Q Note 5), leases not yet commenced start "during the remainder of 2026 through 2036" (Note 9), escrowed supplier funds release "between 2028 and 2030" (Note 4), and Micron's new HBM packaging capacity arrives in 1H CY2027. Management values time over cost: "we believe near-term capacity is more valuable than long-term capacity," and "we still have numerous ROI positive places that we would put compute toward if we had it" (Li, Q2 2026 call).

Buyers are posting commitments and collateral to sellers. Meta's non-cancelable commitments rose from $131.05bn (December 2025) to $349.31bn (June 2026), and Meta moved $10.80bn of money-market funds into restricted cash "related to escrow requirements under certain multi-year infrastructure purchase agreements" (10-Q, Note 4). NVIDIA's own supply commitments rose from $119bn to $279bn in one quarter (NVDA 10-Q).

Funding is the other half of the constraint. Q2 2026 capex was $31.1bn against free cash flow of $784m, and Meta issued $24.91bn of notes in May 2026. Liquidity is not a constraint with $90.26bn of cash and securities, but the marginal gigawatt is now funded with debt, joint-venture equity and leases.

Ad-signal access is the secondary constraint and is not binding at present. Price per ad rose 12% in H1 2026, the fastest full-year or half-year rate since 2021 (Q4 2024 alone was +14%). Signal access last constrained price in 2022, when ATT coincided with price per ad declining 16%, and the 10-Q still says ATT "has negatively impacted, and we expect will continue to negatively impact, the size of the budgets marketers are willing to commit."

Customer-side economics. Marketers "do not have long-term advertising commitments with us" (10-Q Q2 2026). A merchant with a 40-50% product gross margin breaks even on a first order at a return on ad spend of 2.0-2.5x; third-party benchmarks put median Meta ROAS at 1.9-2.2x against 3.3-3.5x on Google Ads (superscale.ai, get-ryze.ai, accessed 2026-09-23 [web, low confidence, small self-selected samples]). At the median, the typical Meta advertiser loses money on the first order and depends on repeat purchases, so Meta's price depends on advertisers' lifetime-value assumptions and on attribution quality, which Apple controls on iOS.▪ Handing budget allocation to Advantage+ raises Meta's control of measurement.

Meta is itself the customer in the accelerator chain. Operating income rose $36.5bn from 2023 to 2025 on cumulative 2023-2025 capex of $139.5bn, a pre-tax return of about 26% [estimate: ignores RL, timing lags and the 2025 useful-life extension].▪ In 2026, capex of $130-145bn comes with operating income guided only above 2025's $83.3bn, while $80.3bn of construction in progress and $347bn of leases not yet commenced have not reached the income statement. Straight-line over 15-20 years, those leases imply about $17-23bn a year of lease cost once commenced [estimate: $347bn ÷ 15-20 years], 20-28% of FY2025 operating income. Price per ad rose about 14% cumulatively from the 2020 level to 2025 (about 2.6% a year) while capex rose 4.6x, so revenue has grown through volume and conversion without passing input-cost inflation through as price.▪

Bargaining power at each interface. - Accelerators: NVIDIA's gross margin held at 72-75% while Meta bought more. Meta is building second sources (AMD 6GW, MTIA more than 1GW, Andromeda running on three chip families), and they have not yet shown up in NVIDIA's margin, which rose 2.6 points y/y. - Memory: power moved to the supplier. Micron expects agreement margins "even at floor pricing levels" to exceed "our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle" (MU 10-Q). - Cloud: mixed. Meta holds about $48bn of neocloud contracts (Nebius $27bn, CoreWeave up to $21bn [web]) and a $14.72bn contingent backstop, and reports of a Meta compute business in July 2026 coincided with declines in Nebius and CoreWeave shares (247wallst, 2026-07-01 [web]). - Power and buildings: financiers and utilities set terms and Meta takes residual risk. Entergy's 10 plants for Hyperion, about $11bn, are paid by Meta over 15 years (Fortune, 2026-03-27 [web]). - Advertisers: Meta's position is intact; price +12% and impressions +14% in Q2 2026. - EssilorLuxottica: holds the retail side. It sold more than 7m Meta glasses in 2025, worth $2.1-2.7bn at $299-379 retail against Meta's total RL revenue of $2,207m, and Meta glasses sales "nearly doubled" in Q2 2026 while Meta's RL revenue grew 16%. Meta bought about 3% of EssilorLuxottica (about €3bn) [web].

Total forward obligations are about $700-750bn: commitments $349bn, unstarted leases $347bn, the two RVGs $41bn and contingent cloud $15bn, with some overlap between the Hyperion lease and the lease pipeline and the RVGs contingent. That is about 6-6.5x FY2025 operating cash flow of $115.8bn, up from about $235bn at December 2025. The AMD warrant ties Meta's effective GPU cost to AMD's share price, which rose 191% year to date partly on the Meta and OpenAI orders; a 50% decline in AMD's price would cost Meta about $50bn of rebate value at full vesting [estimate]. Meta's $14.72bn contingent cloud obligation has the same structure as NVIDIA's $36bn of cloud agreements: both backstop neocloud capacity and shrink only if the provider finds other buyers.

6. Secular and industry trends

6.1 Growth attribution

From 2021 to 2025 Meta's advertising revenue grew with the digital ad market, and all of it came from volume.▪ Ad revenue compounded at 14.3% a year ($114,934M to $196,175M). Impressions rose 1.88x and average price per ad declined about 8% (10-K FY2022-FY2025). The claimed secular driver, AI ranking and Advantage+ raising advertiser returns and therefore price, netted to about zero on price per ad across those four years and shows up only from 2024: price per ad rose 10% in 2024, 9% in 2025 and 12% in each of Q1 and Q2 2026.

The company attributes the 2022-2023 price declines to impressions "in geographies and in products such as video and Reels that monetize at lower rates, and an unfavorable foreign exchange impact" (10-K FY2022). The average price therefore mixes a true per-impression price with surface and regional mix, and the filings do not separate them.▪ The US & Canada share of ad revenue declined from 48.2% in 2020 to 43.5% in 2025.

Against industry dollars. Meta's share of global ad revenue (all media) rose from about 15% in 2021 (GroupM, $763.2bn) to 17.2% in 2025 (WPP Media, $1.14tn) (Marketing Brew, 2025-12-09 [web]), mostly because digital took share from other media. A digital-only share cannot be confirmed from the published agency figures; on GroupM's derived digital totals it was about 23% in both years. The US is measured best:

Meta grew with the closed-loop performance cohort (Amazon, AppLovin, Reddit) from 2023 onward.▪ From 2021 to 2023 Meta ad revenue rose 15% in total (after a 1% decline in 2022) while Amazon ads rose about 50% and Google advertising 14%; the 2022 ATT shock hit Meta harder than any other large peer.

6.2 The 2026 print, and how much of it is the cycle

H1 2026 ad revenue grew 30.1% against a WPP global forecast of +8.9% for 2026. Part is the cycle: 2026 includes the World Cup, the US midterms and an H1 currency tailwind (about 4 points in Q1 and 1 point in Q2), and WPP describes a global ad market at "its highest share of GDP since 1999" [web]. The CFO also cited "improvements in macro conditions relative to Q2 of last year" (Q2 2026 call); the 10-Q attributes the price rise to advertising demand "mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance" and favourable currency. Q2 2026 constant-currency ad growth of 26% against US internet growth of 13.9% in 2025 and WPP's +8.9% is a gap of about 12-17 points that events, currency and macro cannot account for, so most of it is share gain.▪ The Q3 guide of $61-64bn (+19% to +25%, including about a 1-point currency headwind) implies the gap narrows.

What consensus requires. On BBG consensus revenue ($254.1bn, $305.4bn, $361.9bn for 2026-2028) and a global market growing at WPP's 2026 rate and then 7%, Meta's share of global ad revenue goes from 17.2% (2025) to about 20% (2026), 22.5% (2027) and 25% (2028) [estimate: ads at 98% of revenue; 7% for 2027-28 is an assumption]. That is about 2.5 points a year against about 0.75 points a year from 2020 to 2025. The path needs a rising share of digital, material non-ad revenue (under 2% today), or a market growing much faster than agency forecasts.▪

6.3 Technology and regulatory shifts

Slope up: - LLM-based ranking. Self-reported conversion gains; the filed evidence is price per ad growing 9-12% since 2024. - New inventory. Threads ads went global in Q2 2026, and WhatsApp Status ads are "on track toward our global rollout" (Q2 2026 call). - Business messaging and subscriptions. FoA Other revenue $1,007M in Q2 2026, +73%.

Slope down: - AI assistants. ChatGPT ads reached a $1bn run rate in about 200 days, and WPP projects generative-search advertising at $5.1bn in 2026 and over $100bn by 2030 [web]. The first effect lands on search, but conversational commerce also competes with lower-funnel performance ads. - EU signal regulation. Europe was 24.0% of 2025 ad revenue. Europe ad growth decelerated from +39% in Q1 2026 to +24% in Q2 as the revised less-personalised-ads offering rolled out from late Q1; Asia-Pacific decelerated from +29% to +19% in the same quarters, and currency explains part of both. - People growth near its limit. DAP of 3.58bn is about 73% of internet users outside China [estimate: 3.58 ÷ (6.0 − 1.1bn); ITU and CNNIC-derived figures [web]], and DAP grew about as fast as the internet population in the year to June 2026.▪ Australia's under-16 ban removed about 756,000 accounts (Meta newsroom, 2026-08 [web]). - Youth-access rules. The August 2026 settlement imposes a combined 2-hour daily cap and a non-personalised feed option for US minors (Section 18). - Platform gatekeepers. ATT is the precedent: price per ad −16% and US&C ad revenue −1.6% in 2022.

Reality Labs. Glasses revenue is not separately disclosed and Quest revenue is declining, so the filings cannot show whether glasses have reached secular adoption. Category trackers show growth cooling from about 130% to 35% in Q2 2026 (IDC) before the Android XR entry.

7. Critical points

1. The ad business is accelerating while its operating leverage has reversed. Revenue grew 33% in Q1 2026 and 28% in Q2, the fastest since Q3 2021, on impressions +14-19% and price per ad +12%. In the same half, FoA costs rose 56% and the incremental FoA margin was 13% (26% before the Q2 legal and severance charges), against 83% in 2024 and 42% in 2025. On the 2026 expense guide the full-year incremental FoA margin is about 3-13% [estimate]. Employee compensation (+45% in H1 2026 with headcount down 1%), D&A (+46% in Q2), third-party cloud and AI token costs are growing faster than revenue, and most of them are contracted or granted.

2. Free cash flow is near zero and the contracted build extends through 2027. Q2 2026 free cash flow was $784m on $31.1bn of capex (51.1% of revenue). The $130-145bn guide leaves $79-94bn for H2 2026, above H2 operating cash flow at the H1 pace. $81.65bn of commitments fall due in 2027, and Meta has signed $347bn of leases not yet commenced. Consensus free cash flow is −$6.2bn (FY2026E), −$29.2bn (FY2027E) and −$0.9bn (FY2028E); the base model in Section 17 gives −$4.9bn, −$54.6bn and −$41.3bn, and FY2027 is −$55bn to −$63bn in every scenario because 2027 spend is largely contracted.

3. Price per ad compounded about 4% a year over a decade, and the 2024-2026 run is the exception. Price declined in 4 of the 10 years 2016-2025, cumulative price in 2025 was about 3% below 2018 and 8% below 2021, and impressions per person rose while price declined in 2020, 2022 and 2023. 2026 is the first year with both above 10%. The US & Canada price increase of 20% in Q2 2026 is the cleanest evidence that ranking gains raise what advertisers pay; how long it persists decides most of the forward revenue path (Section 17.5).

4. Impression growth in 2026 came partly from ad load. DAP grew 3%, so impressions +16% in H1 2026 required impressions per person of about +12-13%, more than double the 2025 rate of about 5%, and the 10-Q names "the frequency of ads shown". Ad load has a ceiling set by Meta's own tolerance, and the split between time spent and ad load is undisclosed.

5. Off-balance-sheet obligations are about 8-9x on-balance-sheet debt. Notes total $84.0bn, 0.8x trailing EBITDA. Non-cancelable commitments of $349.31bn, $347bn of leases not yet commenced, about $41bn of residual value guarantees and a $14.72bn contingent cloud backstop add to about $700-750bn, 6-6.5x FY2025 operating cash flow, up from about $235bn at December 2025. The signed leases alone have an estimated present value of $180-225bn, which would take lease-adjusted leverage to about 2.6-3.1x trailing EBITDA [estimate, Section 12].

6. Consensus asks for growth that one company at this scale has delivered. Consensus revenue compounds at 21.7% a year over FY2025-FY2028, just above the 90th percentile (20.8%) of three-year outcomes for $150bn-plus companies growing 15% or more. It requires three straight years of $51-57bn of added revenue, which only Amazon has done (2023-2025), from a base 2.6-3.2x larger. Meta's own history points the other way: revenue beat year-end consensus in 12 of 13 years, by a median 8.4%.

7. Reality Labs has absorbed $96.7bn since 2019 and its revenue has been flat for five years. Glasses units rose about 3.8x in 2025 while RL revenue rose 3%, because EssilorLuxottica books most of the retail sale. The 2026 loss is guided "similar to 2025", and 70% of 2026 RL opex goes to wearables.

8. Youth-safety litigation became a cash and product cost in 2026. Legal charges were $2.4bn in Q2 and an expected ~$10bn in Q3 [web]; the August settlement with 52 attorneys general is about $12.7bn fixed over ten years plus $5.3bn contingent, with a combined 2-hour daily cap for US minors. Plaintiffs' stated demands in open cases rose to "more than a trillion dollars" (10-Q Q2 2026), and the under-18 share of DAP, time and revenue is undisclosed.

Management's claims that AI spending is "paying off", that buybacks offset dilution, that the balance sheet remains net cash, that glasses will scale RL and that 2026 operating income will exceed 2025 are tested in Section 8.

8. Management claim pressure tests

"Our AI investments are paying off in the core business" (Q2 2026 call; Goldman Sachs, 30 July 2026: "Core Business Provides Evidence of Near-Term ROIC"). Revenue evidence is strong: ad revenue +27% in Q2 2026 and US & Canada price per ad +20%. At the operating line, FoA incremental margin went from 83% (2024) to 42% (2025) to 13% in H1 2026, and FoA margin from 53.7% (2024) to 43.3% (H1 2026). The 2023-2025 build returned about 26% pre-tax on cumulative capex; H1 2026 FoA operating income rose 8% while capex rose 66%. The disclosed ranking lifts are 1-16% per launch on specific surfaces, Meta's own experiments on the advertiser-budget loop were "not statistically significant" (MS TMT 2026), and how much of the cost increase is frontier-model spend is undisclosed. The claim holds for revenue and is not yet visible in operating income.

"Rising price per ad shows our ad performance improvements" (10-K FY2025: price growth "mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance"). Compounding the disclosed rates, price per ad in 2025 was about 2% above 2019 while impressions rose 2.77x, and over 2022-2025 price explained about 16% of ad growth. The two statements are consistent only if mix dilution from Reels and Asia-Pacific was about as large as like-for-like price gains, and Meta does not disclose the split. The Q2 2026 price gain of 12% included about 1 point of currency on revenue and easier comparisons against a tariff-hit Q2 2025.

"The core social moat is strengthening" (Morgan Stanley, 30 July 2026). FoA's margin premium over Google Services was +10.9 points in FY2025 and −3.0 points in Q2 2026 (about +1-3 before charges). Consolidated ROIC was 44.0% (2021), 35.2% (2025) and 28.6% (trailing to June 2026), and ROIIC on 2025's added capital was about 17%. Engagement is growing and the moat is holding; its returns are declining.

"Advantage+ adoption shows advertisers choosing our automation" (calls, Q4 2024-Q2 2026). The run rate went from $20bn (Q4 2024) to $60bn (Q3 2025) while the product's scope widened from shopping campaigns to all end-to-end objectives and automation became the default setting. Most of the $40bn step coincided with those two changes; the organic share is undisclosed.

"We use buybacks to offset equity compensation" (Susan Li, Q2 2025 call and Goldman Communacopia, September 2025). Meta has bought no shares since August 2025. Class A and B shares outstanding rose from 2,512m (25 July 2025) to 2,548m (24 July 2026), +1.4%, while unrecognised RSU expense rose to $79.79bn. Holding the count flat at $736.60 would need roughly $25-30bn a year of buybacks on top of about $17bn of RSU withholding taxes [estimate], against 2026 free cash flow of roughly −$20bn to +$10bn [estimate, Section 18]. The claim no longer matches behaviour.

"We intend to maintain a positive or neutral net cash balance over time" (Li, Q1 2023 call). Net cash on a notes-only basis declined from $48.8bn (December 2024) to $22.6bn (December 2025) and $6.3bn (June 2026); including operating leases it was about −$22bn at June 2026. In January 2026 Li said external financing "may lead us to eventually maintain a positive net debt balance." Management withdrew the 2023 commitment on that call.

"We are opportunistic buyers of our stock" (Li, Q4 2025 call). Within each year, Meta bought 0.6% more shares over 2017-2025 than equal monthly spending of the same budget would have; 2023 (+11.7%) and 2024 (+10.4%) were good years and 2021 and 2022 (about −4% each) were not. The third of months with the lowest position in the trailing 52-week range received $73.3bn of $174.0bn (42%); months literally in the bottom third of that range received $30.9bn (18%), and the monthly correlation between dollars spent and the discount to the 52-week high is about −0.10. The largest program ($44.8bn in 2021, 77% of that year's operating cash flow) ran near the pre-2023 peak at an average $331, and from November 2025 to August 2026 the stock traded 17-27% below its 52-week high with no purchases. The budget follows residual cash after capex, with a modest price tilt inside the year.

"AI glasses are some of the fastest-growing consumer electronics in history" (Zuckerberg, Q4 2025 call). Units support the claim: EssilorLuxottica sold more than 7m in 2025 against about 2m in 2023-2024 combined. RL revenue rose 3% in 2025. At EssilorLuxottica's reported 10m-unit capacity target, glasses would add about $1.0-2.0bn of RL revenue a year at Meta's $95-200 per unit [estimate]; at 20m units about $1.9-4.0bn, 10-21% of the FY2025 RL loss.

"2026 will likely be the peak Reality Labs loss, and we'll gradually reduce our losses going forward" (Q4 2025 call). RL costs rose every year from 2019 to 2025 ($5,004M to $21,400M). H1 2026 costs were flat (−0.4%) after a 10% RL headcount cut and a VR budget cut of up to 30%, with savings reinvested in wearables [web]; Q2 2026 costs were +3%. Neither 2026 call repeated "similar to 2025", though the 10-Q does. With costs flat, cutting the loss by $2bn needs RL revenue to rise from $2.2bn to at least $4.2bn before hardware costs on the added revenue.▪ The 2022 commitment to "pace" RL investment was met at the consolidated level while RL losses kept rising.

"We expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025" (Q4 2025 through Q2 2026 calls). The statement predates the August settlement. Guided expenses of $165-169bn exclude the expected ~$10bn Q3 accrual, which management said "was not contemplated" [web]. With it and consensus revenue of $254.1bn, 2026 operating income is $75-79bn, 5-10% below 2025's $83,276M [estimate].▪ Revenue of about $258-262bn, the top of the consensus range, would be needed to hold 2025's level. Whether the statement survives the Q3 accrual is unknown until the Q3 print.

"We have compute offers at a significant premium over what we paid" (Zuckerberg, Q2 2026 call). On the same call management said Meta has "nowhere near enough compute" for its own ROI-positive uses, and Meta holds about $48bn of neocloud contracts plus a $14.72bn contingent cloud backstop. Selling capacity at a premium while renting it is consistent only if Meta's own-build cost is well below rental prices. Meta has disclosed no own-build cost per unit of compute, and no compute revenue, price or timeline.

"Meta is a full-stack technology company" (Zuckerberg, Q2 2026 call). Meta scrapped an advanced training chip (reported February 2026), rents Google TPUs, signed 6GW of AMD GPUs and an expanded NVIDIA deal, and pays third-party AI token costs. MTIA covers ranking inference and training at more than 1GW; frontier training runs on merchant GPUs.

Sources: 10-K FY2016-FY2025; earnings calls; Bloomberg daily closes. One-day moves are close-to-close price changes.

The inflections: - Mobile conversion, 2012-2014. Meta rebuilt its products and ad formats for phones while its shares traded below half the IPO price. Revenue compounded at about 51% a year from FY2013 to FY2017 and operating margin rose from 35.6% to 49.7%. Meta bought Instagram and WhatsApp in the same window at prices the market then considered excessive. - Safety and privacy reset, 2018. Capex intensity rose 8.3 points in one year, safety headcount was doubled to 20,000, and the guide cut margins toward the mid-30s. Zuckerberg: "we could choose to decrease our investments in new product areas, but we're not going to" (Q2 2018 call). The mid-30s level was reached only in the year of the FTC fine. - Drawdown and Year of Efficiency, 2021-2023. ATT, TikTok and the metaverse ramp arrived together, headcount rose 20% in 2022 while revenue declined, and three straight quarters of revenue decline followed. The first plan (October 2022) held headcount flat and raised capex; about 11,000 layoffs came two weeks later and the capex cut about three months later. About 21,000 roles and $8.1bn of restructuring charges later, FoA margin recovered 16.4 points, while RL losses rose from $13,717M to $17,729M. - AI capacity pivot, 2025-2026. Capex went from $39bn (2024) to $72bn (2025) toward $130-145bn (2026), financed with $55bn of notes and two joint ventures, and the guide was raised or widened upward at the Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 calls. Zuckerberg: "we need to be a company that builds frontier models" (Q1 2026 call). The outcome is not yet known: Q2 2026 GAAP margin declined 12.1 points y/y and free cash flow approached zero while revenue growth was the strongest in five years.

What the pattern shows. In each downturn Meta's first response was to keep investing; cuts, when they came, applied to non-priority headcount and facilities, and the long-horizon program (VR in 2022, compute and models in 2026) was protected. Meta issues blunt multi-year warnings (mid-30s margins in 2018, the ~$10bn ATT sizing in 2022, "notably larger" capex growth in 2025) that set off one-day declines of 11-26%.▪ In the two resolved cases the outcome was better than the warning (41% 2019 margin ex-fine; 2023 expenses of $88,151M, below the initial $96-101bn guide though inside the later $86-90bn and $88-91bn ranges). Meta copies an attacker's format inside its own apps and accepts lower monetisation per unit of engagement for a period (Stories 2017-2019, Reels 2021-2023), and buys where copying is not possible. Windfalls have gone into the next platform bet: 2020-2021 into hiring and the metaverse, 2023-2024 into the AI capex step. Management's current language also reframes the past: "metaverse" appeared 47 times on the 2021 earnings calls and once on the two 2026 calls, and "superintelligence" 33 times in 2025 and never in 2026, when "Muse" became the label.

10. Management, incentives and capital allocation

10.1 Who runs Meta

Mark Zuckerberg controls Meta with 60.8% of the vote and 13.5% of the economics (342.5m of 2,538.4m shares, 2026 proxy). At $736.60 his stake is worth about $252bn; his 2025 reported pay of $25.1m, almost entirely security and aircraft, is 0.01% of it. The board cannot replace him ("able to exercise voting rights with respect to a majority of the voting power", 10-K FY2025).

Sources: 2026 DEF 14A, Executive Officers; 8-K of 12 January 2026. The 2022 successors to Sandberg, Wehner and Schroepfer were all internal. External hires in 2025-2026 went to government-facing roles (Powell McCormick, Mahoney) and, below officer level, to AI research leadership, where Alexandr Wang arrived as Chief AI Officer after the Scale AI investment. Senior departures in late 2025 included the chief revenue officer (after 11 months in the role), the chief AI scientist and the general counsel. Glassdoor's overall rating declined from 4.4 (January 2025) to 3.7 (March 2026), with CEO approval at 52%, before the May layoff.

The board has 12 nominees, 11 independent. Several directors run companies that buy Meta ads or sell to Meta. Broadcom, whose CEO sat on the audit and privacy committee until the 2026 meeting, received about $500m from Meta in 2023 and about $2.3bn in 2025 (2024 and 2026 proxies, Related Party Transactions).

10.2 What the pay plan rewards

Zuckerberg takes a $1 salary, no bonus and no equity; his reported pay is residence security, a $14m annual pre-tax security allowance paid in cash (unused amounts roll forward), and personal aircraft use, totalling $210.8m over FY2017-FY2025. He has 12.0m Class B shares pledged (3.5% of his holdings) under a board-approved framework.

The other officers are paid mainly in time-vested RSUs (75-85% of 2025 reported pay): an annual grant sized by an "initial equity value" ($20-22m in 2025), vesting quarterly over four years on service alone. There are no performance shares, no relative-TSR hurdle and no holding period beyond ownership guidelines. The cash bonus has company priorities with "no specific weighting or dollar amount" and "full judgment" for the committee; the target was raised from 75% to 200% of salary in February 2025, which lifted target total direct pay to "at or above approximately the 85th percentile" of a peer group that now includes NVIDIA, Oracle and Visa, weighted toward its largest members. There is no severance or change-in-control acceleration, and the clawback is the restatement-triggered minimum. Say-on-pay is triennial; about 89% support in 2025.

Officers hold meaningful stock (Cox about $235m, Olivan about $101m, Bosworth about $63m, Li about $23m at $736.60) and sold under 10b5-1 plans between March and June 2026 (Olivan $11.6m, Li $6.9m, Bosworth $4.8m) with no open-market purchases by any officer or director. CZI-related entities sold about $945m of stock in 2025 [web].

10.3 Candor

Zuckerberg admits operating errors in plain language once the fix is under way: "I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that" on 2022 over-hiring (CNBC, 2026-05-18 [web]), and on the overbuild worst case, "we effectively have just prebuilt for a couple of years, in which case, of course, there would be some loss and depreciation" (Q3 2025 call). He redescribes abandoned strategic positions as continuous. On open source: Llama 3.1 was "an inflection point in the industry where open source AI started to become the industry standard just like Linux" (Q2 2024 call), and "we've always basically said that we were going to do a mix of open and closed" (Q2 2026 call). On Llama 4: "our goal for Llama 4 is to lead" (Q4 2024 call), then "In '25, we rebuilt the foundations of our AI program" (Q4 2025 call), with no mention of Llama on any call since. Internally in July 2026 he said AI agents had not "accelerated in the way that we expected" (TechCrunch, 2026-07-02 [web]); four weeks later on the call: "I'm quite happy with the trajectory that we're on." Questions about return on AI capital receive lists of opportunities without numbers, and Li declined to give a 2027 capex outlook on the Q1 and Q2 2026 calls.

Reality Labs losses, which run through operating cash flow, were $88.1bn in 2019-2025, equal to 55% of the $159.1bn spent on buybacks in the same years.

Per-share outcomes. Revenue per diluted share compounded 26.4% a year from 2016 to 2025 against 24.7% for revenue, because diluted shares declined 12.0% (2,925m to 2,574m). Free cash flow per share compounded 17.8%, about 9 points a year slower than revenue per share, because capex rose from 17.4% to 35.9% of revenue. Free cash flow less stock compensation grew 7.1% a year from 2020 to 2025 against 18.5% for revenue. In H1 2026 free cash flow declined 30% while revenue grew about 30%, and the share count rose. Meta retired 635m shares for $174.0bn (average $274); those shares are worth $467.7bn at $736.60, a money-weighted return of about 24% a year that reflects the stock's rise.

Stated framework against behaviour. Meta has never published a hurdle rate or return target. Li in September 2025: "if we evaluated new projects relative to our existing business, a lot of projects would frankly look not as attractive", and Meta focuses on "growing like operating profit dollars more than sort of any other metric" (Goldman Communacopia 2025). An objective of operating-profit dollars lets returns on incremental capital decline as long as absolute profit rises. The capex framework also moved. Capex was to "come down as a percent of revenue over the long term" (Li, Q3 2022 call), and by Q4 2024 it was "really too early to determine what long-run capital intensity is going to look like."▪ The dividend was held at $0.525 a quarter in 2026 [estimate: rate inferred from payments], after Li's September 2025 reference to "growing our dividend program over time". H1 2026 payments rose 1.6%, in line with the share count.

11. M&A, divestitures and deal track record

Instagram (2012) and WhatsApp (2014), Meta's two successful large acquisitions, account for $17.7bn of accounting consideration and 64% of the $24.5bn goodwill balance at December 2025, and both have billions of daily users.▪ Oculus ($1.85bn, 2014) became Reality Labs, which lost $96.7bn from 2019 through June 2026. Outside those three, most deals with a known outcome were shut down, spun back to founders, forced out by a regulator or absorbed into RL. No deal was large enough to threaten the business. The stock issued for the three large deals has been repurchased (Class A and B shares were 2,549.7m in January 2014 and 2,547.5m in July 2026), and M&A has been a minor use of cash: $8.6bn of cash acquisitions over 2016-2025, 1.6% of operating cash flow (Section 10.4).

Meta has never recorded a goodwill impairment ("no impairment of goodwill has been identified", 10-K FY2025), and the test design explains part of that. Until Q4 2021 there was one reporting unit; at the segment split only $610m of the then $19.07bn goodwill balance went to RL, although Oculus alone generated $1,533M; and failed deals leave their goodwill in FoA, whose goodwill moved by −$4m in 2023, the year Kustomer was spun out. Meta has never published a synergy target for any deal.

WhatsApp was bought at about 560x annualised revenue when Meta itself traded at about 17x FY2014 revenue [estimate]; the 178m shares and 46m RSUs issued would be worth about $165bn at $736.60 [estimate: 224m × $736.60], against FoA Other revenue of $2,584M in FY2025. Instagram's revenue has never been reported; Bloomberg reported about $20bn of 2019 ad revenue [web] and eMarketer estimates $32.0bn of 2025 US ad revenue, 50.3% of Meta's US total [web]. Regulators intervened in three of the seven acquisitions since 2019 with a reported price: the CMA forced Giphy out, the FTC challenged Within (and lost), and China's NDRC blocked Manus. Since 2020 antitrust constraints have led Meta toward structures that record no goodwill; in 2025, non-marketable equity purchases ($18.33bn) were larger than all business combinations ($4.54bn). H1 2026 goodwill acquired was $41m, while equity-method ventures rose from $7.45bn to $9.41bn.

12. Capitalisation and balance sheet

12.1 The debt stack

Meta funds itself with $84.0bn of fixed-rate senior unsecured notes issued by the parent: 26 tranches maturing 2027-2066, with no financial covenants, no security and no subsidiary guarantees ("We are not subject to any financial covenants under the Notes", 10-Q Q2 2026, Note 8). There is no revolver (the $2.0bn facility was terminated undrawn in December 2020) and no commercial paper. Ratings are Aa3 (Moody's, affirmed stable 27 February 2026 [web]) and AA- (S&P).

Sources: 10-K FY2022 Note 11; FWP pricing term sheets of May 2023, August 2024, November 2025 and May 2026. The total reconciles to the 10-Q Q2 2026 Note 8 table ($84,000M face, $83,664M carrying).

Weighted-average cost of debt = Σ(principal × coupon) ÷ Σ principal = $4.36bn ÷ $84.0bn = 5.19%. Every tranche is fixed-rate with no converts, so the cash interest rate equals the coupon.

The weighted coupon was 4.96% at December 2025 before the May 2026 issue; by issue date it is 4.04% (Aug-2022), 5.23% (May-2023), 5.10% (Aug-2024), 5.14% (Nov-2025) and 5.73% (May-2026). The weighted remaining life is about 18.7 years, and the notes traded at 94.9% of face at June 2026. Interest expense net of capitalisation was $1.09bn in FY2025 and $754m in Q2 2026; about $0.2bn was capitalised into construction in progress in Q2 2026 [estimate].

Maturity wall and refinancing. Maturities are $2.75bn in 2027, $1.5bn in 2028, $1.0bn in 2029 and $5.0bn in 2030, 12% of face through 2030; 42% matures after 2046. Refinancing the August 2027 3.50% notes at the May 2026 five-year yield (4.553%) adds about $29m a year. The marginal cost of new debt is rising: between the November 2025 and May 2026 issues the 40-year coupon went from 5.750% to 6.450% and the 40-year spread from T+110 to T+147, the 20-year from T+88 to T+122 and the 10-year from T+78 to T+90, while the 5-year moved from T+50 to T+53.

On-balance-sheet operating lease liabilities were $28.65bn at June 2026 (weighted discount rate 4.3% and term 12.3 years at December 2025). Finance lease liabilities were $1.18bn at December 2025. Meta has no defined-benefit pension.

Sources: 10-K FY2023-FY2025 and 10-Qs. Commitments are "mostly related to third-party cloud capacity arrangements and investments in servers and network infrastructure, data centers, and consumer hardware products in Reality Labs", with $53.52bn due in 2026 and $81.65bn in 2027; one quarter (Q2 2026) added $34bn to the 2027 figure. The unstarted leases commence from late 2026 through 2036 with terms of up to 30 years; the July 2026 leases (about $68bn) commence in 2027-2028 on 18-20 year terms. Their present value once commenced is about $180-225bn [estimate: $347bn undiscounted; level payments over 18-20 years at 4.5-5.5% give 0.60-0.68 of undiscounted, and a 1-3 year commencement lag a further 0.85-0.96, so $177-226bn], 2.1-2.7x the face value of the notes. Some will be finance leases, whose principal falls inside Meta's capex definition.

The Hyperion venture's SPV issued $27.294bn of senior secured amortising bonds due 2049 at 6.581%, rated A+ by S&P (IFR, businessmodelanalyst, accessed 2026-09-23 [web]), about 140bp above the 5.19% weighted coupon on Meta's own notes. The El Paso SPV (Sopaipilla Investor) placed $12.547bn of 7.534% amortising notes due 2048 at T+287.5 on 27 July 2026, about 95bp over Hyperion (cbonds and Yahoo Finance deal reports [web]; El Paso Matters, 2026-08-09 [web]). Meta's links to both are its 20% equity, its leases and its residual value guarantees; the SPV bonds are senior to Meta's notes with respect to the campus assets. Separately, $10.80bn of money-market funds are held in escrow under multi-year infrastructure purchase agreements until 2028-2030, within $13.55bn of restricted cash excluded from the $90.26bn of cash and securities.

Three tax and legal claims behave like debt: - Unrecognised tax benefits: $18.74bn gross. - IRS notice for 2017-2019: $15.89bn of additional tax plus interest and penalties, mostly on the transfer-pricing issue on which the Tax Court valued the 2010 IP transfer at $7.79bn, $1.48bn above Meta's figure. - New Mexico: the attorney general's stated intent to seek up to $62.85bn in penalties in a trial that began in September 2026.

Meta states that damages sought across its proceedings "could amount to an aggregate of up to hundreds of billions of dollars" (10-Q Q2 2026, Note 9).

12.5 Structural balance-sheet risks, ranked by dollar exposure relative to $90.26bn of liquidity

  1. Fixed off-balance-sheet obligations. $349.31bn of commitments ($135bn due by end-2027), about $347bn of unstarted leases, about $41bn of RVG thresholds and $14.72bn of contingent cloud capacity. They are fixed whatever AI demand turns out to be; resale of surplus compute offsets them only if a market exists.
  2. Funding gap in 2026-2028. At guided 2026 capex and sell-side 2027 capex of $214-243bn, free cash flow is near zero or negative while dividends and RSU taxes need about $23bn a year at the H1 2026 pace. Each $25bn of new notes at 5.7% adds about $1.4bn of annual interest.
  3. Rising marginal cost of capital. Long-dated spreads widened 34-37bp in six months, and JV SPV debt priced at 6.6-7.5%, about 140-235bp above Meta's average coupon.
  4. Litigation and tax. New Mexico up to $62.85bn sought; IRS 2017-2019 notice of $15.89bn plus interest; EU DMA and DSA matters.
  5. Refinancing. $10.25bn through 2030, no covenants, no floating rate, no currency mismatch.

13.3 What drove the numbers

Revenue is volume and price alternating. Price led in 2017, 2021 and 2024; price declined in 2019, 2020, 2022 and 2023 as impressions shifted to Stories, Reels and lower-priced regions. 2022, the only revenue decline, was −1.1% reported and +3.9% in constant currency. Since Q1 2026 impressions and price have both grown at double digits.

Margin moves have named causes. - 2018 (44.6%): costs grew 51% on infrastructure and on safety, security and content review. - 2019 (33.9%): the $5.0bn FTC penalty; 41.0% without it. - 2022 (24.8%): revenue −1.1% against costs +23%, R&D up to 30.3% of revenue, an RL loss of $13,717M and $4.61bn of restructuring; 28.8% without restructuring. - 2023 (34.7%): headcount −22% and $3.45bn of restructuring; 37.2% without it. - 2024 (42.2%): a $1.55bn favourable legal accrual change; 41.2% without it. - 2025 (41.4%): the server useful-life extension cut depreciation by $2.92bn, worth 1.5 points; 40.0% without it.

Gross margin declined from 86.6% (2017) to 78.3% (2022) as data-centre costs grew inside cost of revenue, and recovered to 82.0% by 2025 with the help of the 2022 and 2025 useful-life extensions; D&A rose from 6.8% of revenue in 2021 to 9.3% in 2025.

Q2 2026 broke the margin series. Total costs grew 55% (42% before the $3.58bn of charges): R&D +67% to $21,656M, D&A +46% to $6,356M and stock compensation +58% to $7,658M, against revenue +28%. The 2026 expense guide of $165-169bn is +40% to +44% on FY2025's $117,690M. Q2 GAAP operating income declined 8% y/y and would have risen about 9% without the charges.

Cash conversion declined with capital intensity. Free cash flow over EBITDA went from 0.79x (2016) to 0.43x (2025) as capex rose from 1.9x to 3.9x D&A; free cash flow over net income was 0.72x in 2025 and about 0.56x on a trailing basis to June 2026. Working capital releases cash: receivables declined from 53 to 36 days, and payables rose from 25-39 days (2016-2020) to 90 days (2025) during the data-centre build. Net P&E was $225.7bn at June 2026, up from $147.0bn a year earlier.

Tax is volatile. The rate was 87% in Q3 2025, 10% in Q4 2025, −23% in Q1 2026 and 16% in Q2 2026; FY2025 was 30% reported and 13% excluding the $15.93bn charge. The guide for the rest of 2026 is 15-17%.

Three inflections since FY2025: - Revenue growth: accelerated from 22% (FY2025) to 33% and 28% in the two 2026 quarters, 29% and 27% in constant currency. - FoA margin: declined from 51.6% (FY2025) to 48.1% (Q1 2026) and 38.8% (Q2 2026); the Q1 figure was already 3.8 points below Q1 2025 before any large charge. - Free cash flow: went from $10.9bn a quarter on average in FY2025 to $784m in Q2 2026 as capex reached 51.1% of revenue.

Management's expense guide is conservative when Meta is cutting and close to accurate when it is building, and its initial capex guide has become a minimum.▪ Management stopped giving next-year capex direction in Q2 2026, having given it at the Q2 or Q3 call in each of the previous two years. Street estimates are most dispersed on 2027-2028 capex (FY2027 high-to-low 2.13x) and on depreciation, which together explain most of the 1.51x spread in FY2027 operating income. Over twelve months the street added $43.9bn to CY2027 revenue and $63.8bn to CY2028 revenue while CY2027 and CY2028 GAAP EPS declined 0.7% and 1.8%, because capex, depreciation and expense estimates rose faster than revenue.
